dimension: credential envelopes, key versions, rotation and re-encryption
howToReproduce: Apply the `from` -> `to` replacement in `file`, run `command`, and observe the named case fail. Restore. The three postgres entries run ON THE MAC MINI inside a detached worktree; the laptop's Docker daemon is unreachable by policy and a local run of those three MUST fail to start, which is correct rather than a defect.
notes: One mutation SURVIVED on the first sweep and is recorded below as `cipher-latin1-plaintext`, with the case that was added to kill it. It found a real hole: this adapter opened three non-ASCII fixtures and had never SEALED one, so the write side's text encoding was untested and a mis-encoded seal round-trips inside a process that makes the same mistake twice.

No entry is killed by an assertion that compares two things this tranche controls. The six wire-format entries are killed by ciphertexts produced by `internal-packages/tenancy-database/src/secrets.ts`, which this issue does not edit; the three postgres entries are killed by what a real PostgreSQL returns.

mutations.killedBy: wire-compatibility.test.ts > format 1 wire compatibility with the extraction source > opens an envelope the extraction source sealed: revision 1 under root key version 1
mutations.why: The associated data is what binds a ciphertext to its row. Without it the extraction source's envelopes fail the tag check, and — the sharper half — an envelope lifted to another credential would open.

mutations.killedBy: wire-compatibility.test.ts > opens an envelope the extraction source sealed: revision 7 under root key version 2, same key bytes as version 1
mutations.why: The HKDF `info` is the envelope's whole slot identity. A constant derives one key per root key rather than one per envelope, so every stored ciphertext becomes unopenable and two envelopes share a key.

mutations.killedBy: wire-compatibility.test.ts > seals an envelope this adapter can re-open at the same binding
mutations.why: `CredentialSecretVersion_salt_length_check` in the canonical store refuses any other width, so a narrower salt is a row PostgreSQL will not accept.

mutations.killedBy: wire-compatibility.test.ts > seals an envelope this adapter can re-open at the same binding
mutations.why: A 16-byte GCM IV is legal in the primitive and refused by `_nonce_length_check`. It is also the width legacy format 3 uses, so the confusion is one the tree has already had.

mutations.killedBy: key-version-integrity.test.ts > one key version cannot silently open another's envelope > refuses a seal whose handle names a different version than its binding
mutations.why: Silent, permanent data loss on a write that reported success: `open` derives from the BINDING, so an envelope sealed with v2's material under a v1 binding is unsealable forever.

mutations.killedBy: wire-compatibility.test.ts > seals and re-opens multi-byte UTF-8, a newline and a tab
mutations.why: SURVIVED the first sweep and is the reason its killing case exists. Every plaintext this adapter SEALED in a test was ASCII, where utf8 and latin1 agree byte for byte; the only non-ASCII bytes in the tree were in a fixture it opens and never writes. A mis-encoded seal round-trips inside a process that makes the same mistake twice and produces mojibake the day anything else reads the row.

mutations.killedBy: root-key-ring.test.ts > root key handles > refuses to resolve a handle it did not mint
mutations.why: THE OPACITY PROPERTY. `RootKeyHandle`'s brand is a `unique symbol` that is declared and never exported, so nobody can build one — but anybody can CAST `{ rootKeyVersion: 1 }`, which is structurally identical. Resolving by field hands key material to that forgery.

mutations.killedBy: root-key-ring.test.ts > root key ring parsing > refuses a key of the right alphabet and the wrong width
mutations.why: `ROOT_KEY_BYTE_LENGTH` is 32 because AES-256 keys are. A short key would be zero-padded into a weaker key by the decoder, silently.

mutations.to: if (key === undefined) return ok(Object.freeze({ rootKeyVersion: version }) as RootKeyHandle);
mutations.killedBy: key-version-integrity.test.ts > a key removed before its envelopes were re-encrypted fails closed > cannot mint a handle for a version that has left the ring
mutations.why: The fail-closed path. A rotated-out key must make its envelopes UNREADABLE, not readable by whatever the ring answers with instead.

mutations.killedBy: root-key-ring.test.ts > root key ring parsing > refuses a version key that is not an integer literal
mutations.why: `Number(" 1 ")` is 1 and `Number("1.0")` is 1. A ring keyed by " 1" would seal under a version no envelope names.

mutations.killedBy: secret-hasher.test.ts > secret hashing > salts every digest, so the same secret hashes to different strings
mutations.why: Without a per-digest salt, two tenants holding the same secret hold the same digest, and an operator reading the column learns it.

mutations.killedBy: secret-hasher.test.ts > refuses a digest of the wrong width rather than throwing out of the port
mutations.why: `timingSafeEqual` THROWS on mismatched lengths. A throw crossing a port boundary is a defect, not an outcome — a 500 where a refusal belongs.

mutations.killedBy: secret-hasher.test.ts > refuses an unparseable digest instead of answering false
mutations.why: `false` says the secret is wrong, and a caller acting on it rotates a credential that was never wrong. An unreadable row is a different fact.

mutations.killedBy: secret-hasher.test.ts > carries the cost parameters in the digest so an older one still verifies
mutations.why: The cost is IN the digest so a row written before the parameters were raised still verifies. A verifier assuming today's constants rejects every older row, and the rejection is indistinguishable from a wrong secret.

mutations.killedBy: probe-cache-eviction.test.ts > the cache key moves when the material does > changes on a rotation even though the row identifier does not
mutations.why: THIS MUTATION IS THE DEFECT AS FOUND. It restores exactly what `check-provider-health.ts` and `discover-models.ts` passed before WIN-259, and the three failures are the staleness that was live: a key rotated because it leaked kept answering `healthy` from a probe made against the leaked material.

mutations.killedBy: probe-cache-eviction.test.ts > a rotated key does not serve the old key's verdict > re-probes after a rotation even when the eviction did nothing
mutations.why: A ROTATION changes neither identifier — it changes the material behind the same credential — so `updatedAt` is the only field that moves. Dropping it re-opens the whole defect for the rotation case while leaving relink covered.

mutations.killedBy: probe-cache-eviction.test.ts > a rotated key does not serve the old key's verdict > re-probes after a relink even when the eviction did nothing
mutations.why: The mirror of the entry above, and the reason the fingerprint carries all three: a relink at the same instant moves only the credential.

mutations.command: REAL POSTGRESQL, ON THE MAC MINI: pnpm --filter @platos/adapter-postgres-tenancy exec vitest run secrets-key-version.integration --no-file-parallelism
mutations.killedBy: secrets-key-version.integration.test.ts > a real envelope survives a real PostgreSQL round trip > returns every byte of a format-1 envelope unchanged
mutations.why: A truncating decoder makes every stored envelope permanently unopenable, and NOTHING in the crypto suite — which never touches a database — could tell. This is the join the two halves of the proof meet on.

mutations.command: REAL POSTGRESQL, ON THE MAC MINI: pnpm --filter @platos/adapter-postgres-tenancy exec vitest run secrets-key-version.integration --no-file-parallelism
mutations.killedBy: secrets-key-version.integration.test.ts > returns every byte of a format-1 envelope unchanged
mutations.why: The column-swap this suite exists to catch. Every other secrets suite in the directory fills its envelope with `bytes(32, fill)` — a width, not an envelope — and a swap between two same-width fields would compare equal there.

mutations.command: REAL POSTGRESQL, ON THE MAC MINI: pnpm --filter @platos/adapter-postgres-tenancy exec vitest run secrets-key-version.integration --no-file-parallelism
mutations.killedBy: secrets-key-version.integration.test.ts > stores a 35-byte ciphertext beside a 25-byte one without padding either
mutations.why: `rootKeyVersion` is inside the HKDF info AND the associated data, so a store that defaulted it produces a row nothing can open even though every ciphertext byte survived. Every other suite in the directory writes 1 or 2, so a default of 1 would pass all of them; this one writes NINE.
